A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimal-loss estimation experiments, image-generation results using the proposed training schedule, and scaling-law experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds estimator comparisons, sampler and memorization evaluations, training-loss statistics, and a human-preference study.

M1.justification: The DOL/cDOL estimators, Algorithm 1, loss weighting, and adaptive noise schedule remain unchanged. v2's numbered loss-weight equation restates v1's Section 4.2; newly supplied hyperparameters document the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, FFHQ-64, and ImageNet at resolutions 64, 256, and 512 for the same image-generation and loss-estimation coverage. The new CIFAR-10 subset and human assessment of ImageNet-256 outputs extend evaluation procedures within that coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds the previously cited KNN estimator to a direct numerical comparison in Table G.2.1 and adds an EDM2 training-schedule comparator in Table 2. Conversely, the FM noise-prediction and clean-data-prediction comparators in v1's Table 1 and Figure 2(b) are removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include 250-step DDIM/FM sampler evaluations, CIFAR-10 precision/recall measurements, memorization testing on 5,000 CIFAR-10 samples across training epochs, and human preferences from 19 evaluators judging 24 image pairs. Existing generation-training budgets remain unchanged; these are additional evaluation designs.

E4.justification: Appendix G.3 adds training-loss convergence checks, sampler-sensitivity tests, quality-versus-diversity analysis, and longitudinal memorization measurements. The prediction-target ablation in v1's Figure 2(b) is removed. Existing estimator convergence and scaling-law analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 already reports estimator variance and standard deviation. v2 additionally reports means, variances, and standard errors from 150,000 independent training-loss evaluations at four noise levels in Table G.3.1. This does not establish repeated model-training runs; the reported standard errors are inconsistent with the stated variances and sample count.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include cDOL/KNN error rates of 0.04/0.03 and runtimes of approximately 12/67 minutes, sampler-dependent FIDs, precision/recall, memorization rates, and 55.26% human preference for the proposed schedule. Table 2 gains EDM2-schedule results, while FM prediction-target results are removed. Retained headline generation scores and scaling-law results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The principal optimal-loss and consistency theorems, proofs, and importance-sampling bounds are retained. v2 removes the FM noise-prediction and clean-data-prediction conversion derivations from v1's Appendix B.3 and adds an explicit O(L²R) to O(NL) complexity calculation in Appendix G.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: estimating optimal diffusion loss, diagnosing training through loss gaps, improving training schedules, and correcting scaling-law analysis. Contribution bullets are consolidated, but their substantive scope and headline improvement claims remain stable.

C2.justification: New Appendix A distinguishes measuring dataset fit from attaining the empirical optimum, warns about overfitting, and discusses held-out evaluation. Appendix G.3 adds interpretations connecting small-noise fitting to precision and larger-noise fitting to diversity, plus memorization findings. The earlier explanation of velocity prediction through combined noise/data prediction is removed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously missing schedule parameters, including w*=20, a=1/50, and dataset-specific Gaussian means and widths. It also documents loss-estimation sampling, estimator runtimes and CPU resources, and new evaluation procedures. Section 8 promises code and checkpoint release; the PDF does not establish actual availability.

R1.justification: Appendix G.2 expands positioning against the already cited Xu and Niedoba estimators, explaining their relationship to DOL/SNIS and comparing KNN accuracy and efficiency. The Gao et al. work titled Diffusion Meets Flow Matching is removed. Most cited works and the broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain recognizable. v2 revises the loss-gap discussion, moves formulation details into Appendix B, reorganizes experimental subsections, and adds acknowledgments and ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. Affiliations, terminology, and citation style are updated without wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v1's Figure 2 is substantially redrawn as absolute and normalized loss-gap plots, with its prediction-target panel removed. Figure 1's error panel becomes a separate figure. v2 adds multiple result tables, a noise-schedule plot, and generated-image grids, alongside table restructuring and the conference layout; existing convergence and scaling plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Direct estimator comparisons, sampler and memorization checks, and explicit schedule hyperparameters improve evidential support and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the removed prediction-target analysis and new reporting inconsistencies: Table G.3.1's standard errors conflict with its stated variances and sample count, while Section 7 denies human participation despite Appendix G.4's preference study. The net improvement is useful but limited.
